tasks.short: Prepare the returns that environmental and farm rules require, and file them.

steps.what: List the returns due and the figures each one needs.
Pull the accepted totals the return asks for.
Draft the sentences around those totals.

loop.input: return totals and the official template
loop.output: a draft where every figure names its total
loop.check: each figure in the draft equals the totals query; else the draft is discarded
loop.stop: one draft only; if a figure will not tie, stop and leave the form blank
loop.why_not_simpler: the totals are fixed; only the wording changes with the season

steps.what: Correct the draft and sign the return.
File the signed state or federal report.

tasks.design: Accepted totals already in {OPS_SYSTEM} fill the numeric fields of the return. A bounded draft writes the sentences and is kept only when every figure ties to the query. The farm manager corrects and signs. Filing on {GOV_PORTAL} uses that signed version. The portal's own screens stay as they are.
tasks.previous_blocker: The same totals were copied into a workbook and then into the portal, and a mismatch showed up after filing.
tasks.enabler_now: The log now has a query, and a draft can be rejected when a number does not tie.
tasks.still_hard: The portal's questions change, and only the manager knows which total answers which question.
tasks.human_edge: The manager is the person who signs, and who knows when a total should not be filed yet.
tasks.altitude: Copying shrinks. The manager still signs and still files. They do not gain the right to file an untied figure.

reach.task: Post the same period in the ledger
reach.learn: Which totals the return used, so the ledger and the filing match

evidence.claim: Filling a template from a query is deterministic, and a draft that must tie to those figures can be checked by equality.
A generated sentence has invented a source in a published failure of this kind. The tie-out is the control, and a person signs.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: the farm manager signs and files. The bookkeeper owns the ledger. The authority owns the portal.
Structured input: return id, period, measure, total, unit, source batch. Producer is the accepted production log. A measure with no accepted total is left blank, not estimated.
Draft upkeep is extra. Signing time is already in the review step.
unknowns: Which returns does this site actually file, and on which portal?
Is the signatory the farm manager or a director?
research_questions: How often does the portal reject a return that tied internally?

already_counted.description: Correcting and signing the draft is already remaining review time.

incremental.description: Update the template map when a portal question changes.

approvals.approved_version: signed return version; a later edit requires a new signature

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If totals are still a workbook, the pull does not exist and the manager still copies. The tie-out only helps once the log is the source. Provisional.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Inspect houses and equipment, log defects, and see the repair through.

steps.what: Inspect facilities and equipment for disrepair.
Write each defect as a ticket with a place and a photo.
Decide repair now, later, or stop the area.
Do the small repair or assign it.
Close the ticket only after a look at the repair.

tasks.design: Defects become tickets in {WORKFLOW} with a place and a photo, instead of a notebook. The farm manager still walks, still decides whether to stop an area, and still closes the ticket after looking. A stop decision is the version that authorises the work.
tasks.previous_blocker: Defects were a notebook, so the same leak was reported twice and the dangerous ones were not first.
tasks.enabler_now: A ticket with a place, a photo and a status is ordinary workflow software already used for maintenance.
tasks.still_hard: Seeing a crack, and judging whether the house is safe to work in, does not become a form.
tasks.human_edge: The manager is on the ground and can stop work. A ticket cannot.
tasks.altitude: Chasing old notes shrinks. The walk and the safety call stay. Closing a ticket still means the manager looked.

reach.learn: Which ticket is a stop, and which photo is the defect

evidence.claim: A maintenance ticket with status and a photo is standard workflow configuration. The safety call is not.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: the farm manager inspects and can stop an area. A technician does assigned repairs. Facilities leadership owns the capital budget.
Structured input: place, asset, defect, photo, decision (now, later, stop). Producer is the manager on the walk. A ticket with no place is rejected.
The walk is most of the time and stays.
unknowns: Is there already a maintenance workflow, or only a notebook?
Which defects must stop work under the site's own rule?
research_questions: How many tickets are closed without a second look today?

already_counted.description: The second look before close is already remaining review time.

incremental.description: Retire asset names when gear is sold.

approvals.approved_version: repair decision on that ticket; a changed decision needs a new sign-off

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The walk does not shrink. Savings are the notebook and the chasing. If the site has no technician, the manager still does the repair. Provisional.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Keep the farm's financial, production and employment records in one place.

steps.what: Retype production and hours into the workbook.
Post accepted production into the operations record.
Match production and hours to the ledger codes.
Resolve a batch that will not match a code.
Post the matched batch to the ledger.

tasks.design: The retype into a workbook stops. Accepted batches already in {OPS_SYSTEM} and hours already in {HCM} land as fields. The bookkeeper matches them to ledger codes in {ERP}. The farm manager only sees batches that will not match. The bookkeeper posts, and only a batch they have cleared.
tasks.previous_blocker: Three records were kept by copying the same numbers, and employment hours were a separate sheet.
tasks.enabler_now: The accepted log and the timesheet are already structured, so the copy is the step that can disappear.
tasks.still_hard: A lot that was packed for two cost centres still needs a person.
tasks.human_edge: The manager knows which batch was split across customers. The bookkeeper knows the code.
tasks.altitude: Retyping leaves the manager's week. They still decide the odd batch. Posting rights stay with the bookkeeper.

reach.learn: Which production batch is accepted and which code the manager confirmed

evidence.claim: Posting a matched, coded batch is configuration of the ledger. An unmatched batch is an exception, not a guess.
Employment hours are staff data. National works-council rules may require consent before hours are reused beyond pay. The source pack names a Dutch rule; other countries differ.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: the farm manager owns the accepted production log and the exception on a split batch. The bookkeeper owns the ledger posting. Payroll owns pay.
Structured input: batch id, quantity, unit, cost centre, hours, person id, date. Producer is the accepted log and the timesheet. A batch with no cost centre waits. It is not split by a rule.
The retype is eliminated. Bookkeeper matching time is their work, not the manager's saving.
unknowns: Does the timesheet already share person and date fields with the ledger?
Who is allowed to post to the ledger today?
research_questions: What share of batches have no cost centre?

already_counted.description: Exception decisions on unmatched batches are already remaining review time.

incremental.description: Add cost-centre mappings when a new house opens.
Bookkeeper still clears the match each period.

approvals.approved_version: coded batch plus any exception decision; a changed code voids the post

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If the accepted log does not exist yet, the retype cannot be eliminated. Hours may still be restricted by a works council. Provisional.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Keep clerical work, stock, requisitions and marketing asks moving.

steps.what: See open clerical items, stock gaps and asks.
Assign each clerical item to a person and a date.
Raise a requisition when stock is under the line.
Decide a marketing ask that is not a repeat order.
Chase items that missed their date.

tasks.design: Open clerical items and stock gaps show on one list drawn from {EMAIL}, {OPS_SYSTEM} and {PROCUREMENT}. Repeat requisitions under a set line are raised in {PROCUREMENT} for the manager's standing rule. A marketing ask that is not a repeat stays a conversation. Chases go to the office administrator.
tasks.previous_blocker: The work was an inbox and two workbooks, so stock-outs and unanswered asks surfaced late.
tasks.enabler_now: Dates, owners and minimum stock are rules. A mailbox can be sorted into those fields.
tasks.still_hard: A new customer ask, and what the farm should promise, is not a reorder rule.
tasks.human_edge: The manager knows which ask is worth a change to the week list and which is a normal reorder.

ambition.what: Raise a requisition the day a stock line crosses its minimum, including lines that used to wait for a monthly look.

tasks.altitude: Inbox sorting shrinks. The manager still decides new marketing asks. They can change the reorder line; they do not gain a blank cheque to buy.

reach.learn: Which items the manager assigned and which requisitions are already raised

evidence.claim: Minimum-stock requisitions and dated assignments are workflow rules. A new commercial ask is not.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: the farm manager sets the reorder line and assigns clerical work. The buyer places the order. Marketing promises that change the crop stay in the week-list task.
Structured input: item, on-hand, minimum, owner, due date, ask type. Producer is the stock record and the mailbox. An ask with no type waits for the manager.
Reorder lines are upkeep. Assignment review is already counted.
unknowns: Is stock already a quantity per item, or a walk with a clipboard?
What may be reordered without a second signature, and up to what amount?
research_questions: How many 'marketing' mails are actually repeat orders?

already_counted.description: Reading the open list each morning is already remaining review time.

incremental.description: Revise minimums and assignment rules each season.
The office administrator spends time on chases the manager used to send.

approvals.approved_version: stock snapshot against the minimum the manager set

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If stock is a clipboard, the requisition cannot fire and the inbox sort is the only gain. Marketing conversations stay. Provisional.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Returns, defects and records stop being copied. The manager still signs filings, still walks for defects, and still decides a batch that will not code. The bookkeeper posts.
reach: The bookkeeper uses the accepted batch instead of a workbook.
Maintenance works from a ticket with a place.
skills_to_grow: Map a portal question to a total.
Refuse a record that has no place or no code.
role.ambitious_version: A due return is filled from the accepted log, and a defect has an owner the same day.
